title: The generation operation name conflicts with the architecture, the template catalog moves to P6, two document columns are absent from the TSD, and six values this engine needs are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 41 and 43; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T5.3 and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P5-016); ownership.json api and tables (POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents, template and merge_field under P6); legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 3, 4, 9, 12 and 13; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 and R9
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 16 Test cases
description: Six things this story needs are not settled by the sources. (1) The operation name conflicts: the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 name POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents while Architecture v5 slide 16 names POST /documents/generate. (2) The template catalog moves: the legacy story reads a TemplateCatalog inside the document module and TSD P5 T3.1 still gives document.template_id a relation to template, but the Ownership Map gives template and merge_field to P6 in rwb_comms, so the read becomes the RWB-P6-E1046-CON contract. (3) TSD P5 T3.1 has template_id (DF-DOC-032) and treatment_id (DF-DOC-033) and no template_code or template_version column, while legacy section 13 adds all four to the document row and the index is built on treatment_id and the template code. (4) The P3 case read, the S2 treatment read, the P1 source-data merge-field read and the P7 central-ledger read are consumed by this story and its case contract, its S2 contract, its P1 contract and its ledger read appear in no C row of the work package. (5) The field-level names of GenerateRequest, GenerationResult, the Document shape and the four provider interfaces are given only as a sketch in legacy section 12. (6) The PDF/A-2b renderer, the font, the decision code D6.4 with its LOV, the database login, the 24-hour idempotency window, the ten-template bound and the feature flag name are assumed or unstated. The template codes DIL-CONTRACT, DIL-CA, DIL-MORTGAGE and RES-AGREEMENT and the template-to-document-type mapping are assumed by the legacy story itself (DL28, DL19).
evidence: ownership.json 'POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents' basis reads 'Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 ... slide 16 (rwb-document IN: POST /documents/generate) names the path' while the id is the Ownership Map path; slide 16 of the architecture text reads 'REST POST /documents (returns upload link) ... POST /documents/generate'; TSD P5 T3.1 defines DF-DOC-032 template_id and DF-DOC-033 treatment_id and no template code or version column, and legacy section 13 says 'the new columns template_code varchar(30), template_version integer, treatment_id uuid' with the index on (treatment_id, template_code); ownership.json gives template and merge_field to P6 and legacy section 3 names RWB-E1-046 as a P5 precondition; the work package C list is RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P6-E1046-CON and RWB-P7-E1027-CON and names neither S2 nor P1; legacy section 13 says the parameter values are assumed and names the flag rwb.dochub.generation-engine
proposed: Use the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 path /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents on base /api/recovery/document/v1 and record the architecture slide 16 name as the loser (ASM-101); read the template version and the merge field list only through the P6 catalog contract RWB-P6-E1046-CON and hold no template row (ASM-102); add template_code varchar(30) and template_version integer to document beside template_id and treatment_id and build the partial unique index on (treatment_id, template_id) where state is DRAFT and is_active (ASM-103); consume the S2 treatment and P1 source-data contracts and the P7 ledger against published contracts and fakes while leaving the C list exactly as the work package gives it (ASM-104); fix the request, answer and provider shapes in RWB-P5-E2026-CON (ASM-105); keep the template codes and the type mapping as data rows confirmed by Legal and the product owner (ASM-106); render PDF/A-2b with the font as a parameter (ASM-107); write decision code D6.4 with final call GENERATED (ASM-108); refer to the rwb-document login (DP-02) without a name (ASM-109); read the 24-hour window and the ten-template bound as parameters and name the flag rwb.document.generation-engine (ASM-110)

title: The generation contract baseline has no settled operation name, no published provider shapes and two consumed contracts outside the plan
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 41 and 43; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T5.3 and T-A.1/T-A.2; ownership.json api and tables; legacy RWB-E2-026 sections 12 and 14; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.3 Events published; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The baseline has to fix four things the sources leave open. (1) The path: the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 name POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents while Architecture v5 slide 16 names POST /documents/generate, so the declared path is a resolution and not a copy. (2) The provider shapes: legacy section 12 gives TemplateCatalog.current, TemplateCatalog.mergeFields, TreatmentReader.find, MergeFieldProvider.resolve and DecisionLogWriter.write as Java signatures with no field-level answer, and the baseline must publish them as typed contracts whose owners are P6, S2, P3, P1 and P7. (3) The consumed rows: the P3 case contract, the S2 treatment contract, the P1 source-data contract and the P7 central ledger read are consumed by the generation API and are in no C row of the plan, so the baseline declares them as consumed and faked without claiming a plan dependency. (4) The contract elements that carry values: the 24-hour idempotency window and the ten-template bound are parameter names rather than numbers in the document, the message texts are copied from the legacy section 14, and the event schema has five payload fields and no personal data. No source gives the field-level names of TemplateVersion, MergeField, TreatmentSummary and DecisionRecord.
evidence: The architecture text reads 'REST POST /documents (returns upload link) ... POST /documents/generate' on slide 16 while ownership.json declares 'POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents' with x-module P5 from API Specification v4 and TSD P5 API-P5-016; TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-016 gives 'Request GenerateRequest' and 'Response DocumentPage' with no field list; legacy section 12 gives the five interfaces as Java signatures only; the work package C list names no S2 and no P1 contract and names RWB-P7-E1027-CON only; the TSD P5 T3.1 document table and the legacy section 13 give the columns the Document shape claims
proposed: Declare the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 path and record the slide 16 name as the loser (ASM-115); fix the three resources and their required sets as schema constraints so an additive change stays inside major version 1 (ASM-111); publish the four provider interfaces and the decision record as typed contracts with their owners from the Ownership Map (ASM-112); declare one event for this key with five payload fields, no personal data and no file byte, and name DocumentFieldsExtracted only as the service's other event (ASM-113); record the S2, P1 and P7 reads as consumed and faked with the missing C rows carried (ASM-114); carry the message texts and the status mapping as contract elements (ASM-116)

title: The retention-class and legal-hold read surface of rwb-document has no operation, no shape and no document-level hold in any source, and the case and reference contracts it consumes are not in the story's contract list
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-01, DP-05, DP-07, DP-11, DP-13, DP-19); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 41, 42, 43 and 44 (JOB-17, the two P5 events); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (document, document_type, retention_action), T3.2 (LOV-RETENTION-ACTION) and T5.2; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.1 (retention_rule, DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-126); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 (DF-CAS-020 legal_hold); FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.17, A2.18 and section 3 (REQ-DCM-016, REQ-DCM-019, REQ-DCM-020); Program BRD v4 NFR-028 (Open, DL26), NFR-029, NFR-072, NFR-074; Ownership Map tables (document, document_type, retention_rule, retention_action, recovery_case, decision_log_entry, lov_value); WP B-P5-03 story line for RWB-P5-AD021-APP (H three CON rows, C [], I [], X [])
section: Metadata table (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies), section 1 Story, section 3 Preconditions, section 4 Flow, section 8 BR1 to BR8, section 11 Data, 12.1 REST provided, 12.2 REST consumed, 12.6 Schedules, 12.8 Contract fakes, section 13 Solution plan, section 15 Screens and states
description: Five points are unsettled by the sources and are combined into this one row for the app story. First, the legal hold has no document-level home: REQ-DCM-016 and NFR-072 speak of a hold on a case or a document, but the only hold column the sources define is recovery_case.legal_hold (DF-CAS-020) in P3, and the Ownership Map has no document hold table, so the document service must read the case through the P3 case contract and project the flag onto its documents rather than own a hold. Second, the three operations this story consumes (GET /cases/{caseId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold, GET /admin/lists/{listCode}) are P3's and are faked, but the plan gives the story a Contract dependencies list of None, so the C rows that DP-07 and DP-11 would add are absent and only step D1 may change the plan. Third, the identity of the class as a resource and the paths of the class and document-retention reads are the baseline's design: no source names /retention-classes, /documents/{id}/retention or /documents/{id}/retention-actions, and their query parameters and answer field names are not named either. Fourth, the retention periods, age bases and end actions are unset: the Program BRD records NFR-028 as Open under DL26 (retention classes defined per type, periods not set), so no number may be written in code or in a test. Fifth, the run that produces the actions is not this story's: JOB-17 is a Temporal Schedule of rwb-document (Architecture v5 slide 44) whose workflow and operations belong to RWB-P5-E1017-APP, so the story reads the outcome and starts nothing. A sixth, smaller point is carried too: the per-service database login name is not given by any source (DP-02), and the run summary message MSG-P1-020 names a case count without a text.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 row '| DF-CAS-020 | legal_hold | BOOLEAN | boolean | Yes | None | Workbench |' is the only hold column; Ownership Map tables list no hold table and give recovery_case to P3; WP B-P5-03 story line for RWB-P5-AD021-APP holds C [] while 12.2 of the story names three P3 rows; Program BRD v4 line 'NFR-028 ... Retention classes defined per type; periods not set | Open, DL26'; Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-17 | Retention | monthly, 1st Sunday | rwb-document | Schedule' and slide 41 P5 OUT 'topic rwb.document.events.v1: DocumentStored, DocumentFieldsExtracted'; FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-017-02 (the DOCRET decision record) and AC-EXC-P5-017-02 (RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING).
area: Document (P5) retention classes and legal hold: hold ownership, consumed contracts, read paths, unset periods and the run
owner_role: Solution architect, with the Compliance and PDPA officer role owner and the P3 and P5 service owners
proposed: Read recovery_case.legal_hold through the P3 case contract on every read and project it onto the document as legalHold and legalHoldRef, with no hold table and no hold write in rwb_document; keep the plan's C list as None, build against the three P3 fakes and record the missing rows for step D1; fix the four read paths, their queries and their answers in the RWB-P5-AD021-CON baseline and treat them as not specified in the sources; keep every period, age basis and end action as a class-load data row of RWB-P5-E1041-APP and let a missing class fail as 422 rather than default; read the retention_action rows and the DOCRET reference the run wrote and start, stop or re-run nothing, since JOB-17 belongs to RWB-P5-E1017-APP.

title: The contract baseline of the retention-class and legal-hold surface fixes paths, shapes, statuses and a hold projection that no source names, and it consumes three P3 rows the plan does not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-01, DP-05, DP-07, DP-11, DP-13, DP-19) and §R7.2 s12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 41, 42, 43 and 44; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T5.3; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.1; Ownership Map tables and API (POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold is P3); FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.17 and section 3; WP B-P5-03 story line for RWB-P5-AD021-CON (H, C, I and X all empty; ready Day 1)
section: Section 1 Story, section 2 Business rationale, section 3 Preconditions, 12.1 REST provided, 12.2 REST consumed, 12.3 to 12.6, 12.8 Contract fakes, section 14 Validation and messages, section 18 Traceability
description: A contract baseline has to fix what it publishes, and six points here are fixed by this baseline rather than by a source. First, the paths and query parameters of the four reads (/retention-classes, /retention-classes/{classCode}, /documents/{documentId}/retention, /documents/{documentId}/retention-actions) are not named anywhere, and neither are the field sets of RetentionClassPage and RetentionActionPage. Second, the admin load and the run of the same surface have no contract story of their own in this WP: RWB-P5-E1041-CON covers the class load and RWB-P5-E1017-APP the run, so the baseline declares RetentionLoad, RetentionLoadResult, RetentionRun and RetentionRunPage as shapes and claims none of the four admin operations. Third, the legal hold is a case attribute (DF-CAS-020) with no document-level hold table, so DocumentRetention carries a projected legalHold and legalHoldRef and the contract declares no hold write, while POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold stays P3's. Fourth, the plan gives this story no H, C, I or X row, yet three P3 rows are consumed and faked, so the C entries that DP-07 and DP-11 would add are absent and only step D1 may change the plan. Fifth, the status mapping per read and the text of MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P2-006 and MSG-P1-020 are not stated per operation in the sources: the statuses are carried from the legacy endpoints of the key and the three texts are marked as not specified. Sixth, the LOV-RETENTION value set is not enumerated in any source: the two class codes the legacy criteria use (LEGAL10Y, GENERAL05Y) are fixtures, not a list definition, and the class periods stay unset under DL26.
evidence: WP B-P5-03 story line for RWB-P5-AD021-CON with H [], C [], I [], X [], ready 'Day 1'; WP story line for RWB-P5-AD021-APP with C []; Ownership Map API 'POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold ... owner P3' and tables 'recovery_case P3', 'lov_value P3'; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 DF-CAS-020 legal_hold; TSD P5 v2 T3.2 'LOV-RETENTION-ACTION | ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD, EXCEPTION' (the only enumerated list of the surface); Program BRD v4 NFR-028 'Open, DL26'; FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-017-02 and AC-ALT-P5-017-01 for the LEGAL10Y and GENERAL05Y values; Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility within a major version).
area: Document (P5) retention contract baseline: unpublished paths and shapes, unclaimed admin operations, the projected hold and the missing P3 contract rows
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-document, with the solution architect and the P3 owner
proposed: Publish the four reads and the four resources on /api/recovery/document/v1 with the class-in-force rule, the projected hold, the LOV-RETENTION-ACTION values and the DOCRET reference; declare RetentionLoad, RetentionLoadResult, RetentionRun and RetentionRunPage as shapes and name the four admin operations as RWB-P5-E1041-CON's and RWB-P5-E1017-APP's, claiming none of them; carry the three P3 rows as consumed with owner, 2 s budget and fakes and record the missing C entries for step D1; fix the status mapping per read and mark the three message texts and the LOV-RETENTION value set as not specified in the sources; declare no event, no workflow and no Schedule, name JOB-17 with its owner, and fail the drift test on any fake that departs from the document.

title: The secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-007 has no legacy AC and several document-hub values of the outbound path are not fixed in the sources
source: WP B-P5-03 story line RWB-P5-E1007-APP (acs [], secondary true, C RWB-P2-E1007-CON, X []); legacy story RWB-E1-007 sections 1-19; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.1, A2.3 and A2.17; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 and T-A.1; Arch v5 slides 11, 16, 37, 41 and 44
description: This story is the secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-007: it owns no legacy acceptance criterion (AC1-AC7 belong to RWB-P2-E1007-APP) and its six criteria are new under D-RCV-60, so the origin of the criteria and the split itself have no source line. On the document-hub side several values the slice needs are not fixed in the sources: the deliverFile manifest and claim-check field names are rwb-integration's contract and not written in the FSD or TSD; the document type an outbound interface file is stored under, and therefore its retention class, is a data row of the type table that the six agreed types do not name; the case that anchors document.case_id for a batch file of 85 notices on 85 cases is not stated; no 404 message ID exists; the login name and the feature-flag name are not specified; the 15-minute link comes from the architecture and not from a business source; RWB-PLT-TE012-APP is used although the story JSON lists no X dependency; and the rwb-case read is consumed although it is not in the C list. Each default applied is recorded as ASM-B-P5-03-E1007-101 to -109.
evidence: WP B-P5-03 line 58: acs [] and secondary true. Legacy RWB-E1-007 section 11 names DF-DOC-006 document.storage_ref only; section 12 names the four jobs and two admin endpoints. FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 names the six types (DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, APPRAISAL_REPORT, TITLE_DEED, SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT, GUARANTOR_NOTICE); no outbound file type is among them. Arch v5 slide 11: manifest fileId, batchId, sha256, record count and a SAS link for one file, 15 minutes.
area: Contract and data of the document-hub side of the outbound-file path (P5)
owner_role: Solution architect (P5 document hub, with the rwb-integration contract owner)
proposed: Treat the slice as new work under D-RCV-60 with six new criteria and no legacy AC; take the manifest and claim-check field names from RWB-P2-E1007-CON; read the type code and the retention class from document_type in force and leave the outbound type row to the type-table load with the placeholder of this gap; anchor document.case_id on the case ID the store request carries and carry the 85 case IDs in the manifest; use the 15-minute link of Arch v5 slide 11 as a property CLAIM_CHECK_MINUTES = 15; build and test against the RWB-P5-E1024-APP store fake, the rwb-case contract fake and the RWB-PLT-TE012-APP stub; refer to the rwb-document login (DP-02) without a name; confirm every default at the contract review of the two slices.

title: The secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-016 owns no legacy AC, and the DP10 catalog composition, the retention-class operation path and answer, the consumed contracts, the login and the product code are not fixed as this slice needs them
source: WP B-P5-03 story line RWB-P5-E1016-APP (acs [], secondary true, H/C/I/X all [], patterns DP01, DP02, DP05, DP07, DP08, DP11, DP19); legacy RWB-E1-016 sections 2, 3, 4, 7, 11, 12 and 19; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 41, 43 and 44; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 and T-A; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A1.4 and A2.17; Ownership Map (tables and rulings); RWB-ITG-E1016-ITG sections 2, 3 and 12.2
description: This story is the secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-016 and it owns no legacy acceptance criterion (the P1 slice, the P4 slice and RWB-ITG-E1016-ITG carry AC1 to AC11), so the split itself and the origin of the six new criteria have no source line. Beyond the split, eight points are open. (1) The composed catalog entry of a data product is split by the ownership rulings: P1 owns data_product, data_product_access, sys_objects and sys_fields, P4 owns the roles, the scope and the masking policy, and P5 owns retention_rule, yet no source names the composed entry as one contract or states that the P5 part is served as a separate read. (2) No source names the operation that exposes the retention class, its path, or that it is a product-scoped list plus one read by class code; the shared shape of RWB-P5-AD021-CON is this run's own construct. (3) The field-level names of the retention-class answer are not fixed by any source, and neither is the paging shape of the list. (4) The four operations this slice consumes (rwb-access authorise and permissions, the rwb-case case read, the rwb-source-data data-dictionary read) are real contracts, but the story's contract dependency list is None, so they are consumed as fakes and the C entries are missing. (5) DP-08 and DP-19 name platform contracts in the DP table (H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) while the story's H list is None: the guard is the service template's and the gateway route is not built here. (6) No source names the per-service database login. (7) The mapping of the product code DP10 to the document data product is not stated in any source; the eleven tables behind it are P5's under the Ownership Map. (8) No source names a feature flag for this slice. Each default applied is recorded as ASM-B-P5-03-E1016-101 to -109.
evidence: WP B-P5-03 story line RWB-P5-E1016-APP: acs [], secondary true, H [] , C [], I [], X []; legacy RWB-E1-016 AC1-AC11 and section 12 (GET /data-products/{productCode}/records, GET /admin/data-products, the in-process interfaces DataProductAccessLoader, CaseScopeQuery and FieldMasker); Architecture v5 slides 14 and 16 (P4 IN surface; P5 IN/OUT without a retention operation), slide 41 (P5 owns retention, P4 owns roles, scope, masking and access log, P1 owns the ACE view contract) and slide 44 (JOB-17 retention on rwb-document); Ownership Map rulings ASM-A6-tables-10 (retention_rule to P5, P1 drops its copy) and ASM-A6-tables-5 (reference data to P3); TSD P5 T-A.1 lists 17 document endpoints and none for the retention class or the catalog; TSD P5 T3.1 defines retention_rule columns (DF-REF-116 to -126) but no answer shape; FSD P5 A2.17 gives the class values LEGAL10Y, GENERAL05Y, rule version RET-2026.11 and the exception RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING but no API; RWB-ITG-E1016-ITG sections 2 and 12.2 require a P5 retention contract without naming it; no source states a login name, a DP10 mapping or a flag name.
area: rwb-document access, retention contract and catalog composition
proposed: Accept the six new criteria as the P5 deliverable and record the split in the story; publish GET /api/recovery/document/v1/retention-classes and GET /api/recovery/document/v1/retention-classes/{classCode} with the shared RetentionClass shape of RWB-P5-AD021-CON, so the ITG suite joins the P5 class to the P1 entry by product code; consume the four P4, P3 and P1 operations as published contracts with their fakes and add the four missing C entries at the verification loop; inherit the guard library and the gateway route from the service template and add no H dependency; refer to the login as the rwb-document login (DP-02) until the DBA names it; fix the product code DP10 for the document product and the flag rwb.document.access, and confirm both in the verification loop.

title: The P5 retention slice has no source value for its retention periods, its document age basis, its retention-load and run-read paths, its archive container name and its login, and the three contracts it consumes at run time are not in its contract-dependency list
source: RWB-E1-017 sections 3, 4, 11, 12, 13 and 14; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.17 and REQ-DCM-019; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and the NFR table; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.1 (retention_rule) and T3.2 (LOV-RETENTION-END); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 44 (JOB-17); Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-10; Decision Log DL26; WP B-P5-03 story line for RWB-P5-E1017-APP (H [], C [RWB-P1-E1017-CON])
section: Metadata table (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies), section 1 Story, section 3 Preconditions, section 7 Acceptance criteria, section 11 Data, 12.1, 12.2, 12.6, 12.8, section 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story set the retention periods, the age-basis fields and the archive location as rule rows, and left the periods open under DL26. For the P5 slice no source states which tables, which age basis and which months the documents of product DP10 carry, no source names the retention-load, retention-approval, run-read and rerun paths of the target service, no source names the write-once archive container or fixes its immutability policy, and no source names the per-service database login. The story also consumes three contracts at run time that its dependency list does not carry: the P3 case and legal-hold contract (recovery_case.legal_hold, DF-CAS-020, and case_no, DF-CAS-002), the P3 reference-data contract (LOV-RETENTION, LOV-RETENTION-END) and the P7 decision-record contract (the DOCRET record and its collection into the central ledger); the plan's list holds RWB-P1-E1017-CON only. Finally, the DP table of Template and Rules v1 R5.5 adds five H rows (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) to the patterns the story applies while the plan's build list is empty, because this is a secondary slice of a key already split across P1, P5, P7 and RWB-ITG-E1017-ITG. The story resolves each point with a recorded default, keeps every legacy value character for character, and marks every value it fixes as a default rather than a source value.
evidence: RWB-E1-017 section 3 'Retention rule version "RET-2026.11" is loaded and approved: DP05 interaction at 24 months on occurred_at (assumed until Compliance supplies the bank schedule; DL26)' and section 12 'Trigger Quartz cron 0 30 2 ? * SUN#1, Asia/Bangkok'; Decision Log v10 DL26 (retention and masking periods, owner Compliance, status open); TSD P5 v2 NFR-028 'periods not set' and NFR-031 'Not set, DL26'; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 'LOV-RETENTION-END | ARCHIVE, REVIEW'; Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-17 | Retention | monthly, 1st Sunday | rwb-document | Schedule'; Ownership Map tables retention_rule ruling 'Retention is P5 rwb-document ...; P1 drops its retention_rule copy' (ASM-A6-tables-10); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-07, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19; WP B-P5-03 story line for RWB-P5-E1017-APP with H [] and C ['RWB-P1-E1017-CON'].
area: Document (P5) retention and archive: periods, age basis, admin paths, archive container, login and consumed contracts
owner_role: Solution architect, with the Compliance and PDPA officer and the platform storage owner
proposed: Build the P5 slice on the recorded defaults: RET-2026.11 at 24 months for DP10 documents on created_at with end action ARCHIVE until Compliance supplies the bank schedule (DL26); the shared retention contract shape of RWB-P5-AD021-CON for the retention-class and document-retention reads, with the four admin operations on /api/recovery/document/v1; the write-once container rwb-docs-archive of RWB-PLT-TE012-APP with a manifest of row count and SHA-256 per file; the phrase 'the rwb-document login (DP-02)'; and the P3 case, P3 reference-data and P7 decision-record contracts named in 12.2 and 12.8 with their fakes. When Compliance supplies the schedule, load it as a new rule version with no code change; when the platform and contract owners publish, add the five H rows and the three consumed contracts to the plan, re-run the dependency check and swap each fake for the real contract in the same iteration.
